title: Slimline runtime bases and tiered build-cache roles to reduce CI latency and image churn
creator: Marco Liu
description:
Problem: Our CI fleet currently builds and stores ~12 different Docker base images across multiple services. Each repository maintains slightly different base variants (node, python slim, python full, golang toolchain layered, etc.), which increases image churn, CI cache misses, and inattentive toolchain drift. That churn inflates CI latency on cold runs, increases S3/CAS storage costs, and complicates security patching.

Goal: Consolidate to two slim, well-documented base images ("slim-runtime" and "slim-builder") and introduce explicit cache tiers and roles (local ephemeral cache, shared CAS/remote-cache, and primed warm images) to reduce cold CI times, cut image storage, and standardize toolchain upgrades. As part of the work we will stage lint/toolchain upgrades so we reduce flakes and maintain hermetic builds.

Scope: repository-level Dockerfile migration guidelines, a migration script, CI template updates (Buildkite), central registry tagging policy, caching profiles for Buildkite and remote CAS, and a rollout plan with canary repos. Excludes on-prem private deployments (tracked in ENG-98770).
acceptance_criteria: Two official base images published to our internal registry: registry.redwood-inference/slim-runtime:stable and registry.redwood-inference/slim-builder:stable
CI templates updated to use cache profiles; cold build median latency reduced by >=30% for targeted repos during canary period
All service repositories in first wave (15 repos) migrated with automated scanner and PR templates
Toolchain (node/python/golang) upgrades managed via pinned manifest; at least one repo validated with new lint/toolchain and no regressions in tests
Rollback path: repos can opt back into previous base image via a single CI variable and metrics dashboards show no regression after rollback
tasks: Audit current base image variants across 120 repos (scripted inventory)
Design two base images and publish Dockerfiles to infra/base-images repo
Add cache-profile support to shared Buildkite pipeline templates and document usage
Create migration automation: scanner that opens PRs to replace FROM lines and update pinned toolchains
Run canary migration on 15 low-risk services and measure CI latency/storage changes
Rollout remaining repos in waves, monitor, and address flakiness
Update security scan baseline and re-run image vulnerability scan for new images
Document deprecation schedule for legacy bases and notify teams
technical_notes: Base image choices: slim-runtime starts from debian:bookworm-slim + tzdata + ca-certificates + minimal libc deps; slim-builder extends slim-runtime and includes build-essential, python3-dev, gcc, go 1.20 and node 18 (pinned via nvm shim)
Build flags: use BuildKit; enable inline cache export/import --cache-to=type=registry,ref=${REGISTRY}/${IMAGE}:cache,mode=max --cache-from=type=registry,ref=${REGISTRY}/${IMAGE}:cache
CAS config: remote cache backed by our internal registry and GCS for compressed layers; TTL for primed caches set to 14 days initially
Priming strategy: weekly cron job that builds slim-builder with common package combinations and pushes cache tag; warm images retained for top-20 active repos
Hermetic builds: ensure reproducible layer ordering and use lockfiles for pip/npm/go modules; output deterministic artifact manifests
Lint/toolchain upgrade: follow blue/green approach — pin old toolchain via TOOLS_TAG and expose NEW_TOOLS=true to opt-in per-repo CI
progress_updates: 2026-02-20: Inventory script completed across 123 repositories; identified 11 distinct base variants and 9 repos already using custom hardened bases
2026-02-26: Prototype base images built and pushed to sandbox registry (registry.sandbox.redwood-inference/slim-runtime:20260226); initial security scan passed medium threshold
2026-03-03: Buildkite templates extended with cache-profile param and tested on infra/tools repo; observed cold-build reduction ~22% for a node service
2026-03-08: Migration scanner PoC opened PRs against three canary repos (GH PRs #12234, #12236, #12241); two merged after minor test fixes
2026-03-11: Canary metrics dashboard created in Grafana showing build duration, tokenized cache hit rate, and registry storage delta (dash link below)
review_feedback: Aisha Raman (security): ask to ensure image is built with non-root user and to add runtime seccomp profile — actioned in slim-runtime Dockerfile
Diego Marquez (platform): prefer keeping a small compatibility shim for legacy apt packages for two repos that depend on stretched libs — added recipe and compatibility layer in slim-builder
Priya Nair (devex): request to add a CLI flag to migration tool to opt-out if repo has bespoke build steps — added --force and --dry-run modes
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Some repos have native compiled extensions that break on slim-builder. Mitigation: add preflight test in scanner and allow 'legacy' opt-out label, plus a one-off builder image with older glibc for affected repos
Risk: Remote CAS cold-miss spike on rollout. Mitigation: staged rollout with priming job for top 20 repos and temporary increase of cache TTL
Risk: Lint/toolchain regressions. Mitigation: opt-in per-repo for new toolchain, automated test matrix runs in parallel and mandatory integration tests for core infra repos
notes_for_followup: Add a short RFC describing base image lifecycle and CVE response plan to get legal/security sign-off
Coordinate with SRE to add build latency SLOs to the console per-repo team pages
Plan a retro after wave 2 to capture blocker themes and adjust migration scanner heuristics
